bug_semantics: The default object.to_json builtin recursively serializes IList/array elements and object members through a static local WriteValue function without a recursion-depth limit, execution-stack guard, or circular-reference detection. A template can create a ScriptObject that points to itself and pass it to object.to_json; WriteValue then revisits the same object until .NET raises the fatal, effectively uncatchable StackOverflowException, terminating the host process. Deep acyclic input can exhaust the stack by the same path.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable ToJson/WriteValue implementation was first written in PR #533 member commit a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f. GitHub landed PR #533 as the one-parent squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1, but the retained eight-member PR chain and identical head/squash trees permit decomposition; the second member is the smallest commit that adds object.to_json and both unchecked recursive calls.
ai_marker: absent — BIC commit object has no AI author/co-author/Generated-with marker; see evidence
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-xcx6-vp38-8hr5 documents the one-line PoC {{ x = {}; x.self = x; x | object.to_json }}, traces ToJson to the unchecked recursive WriteValue calls, and identifies fatal StackOverflowException process termination. It lists patched version 7.0.0; its package range says <=5.16.0, while the alias bundle describes all versions before 7.0.0.

In the clone, `git log -L 494,530:src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1` attributes the complete vulnerable WriteValue body to squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1. PR #533's retained chain is reproduced by `git rev-list --reverse 0e777fe3c747e9ac4d774b8513e092ff3054ce34^..63af24e80597d88289df5f92c6286e10868378ec`; `git rev-parse f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1^{tree} 63af24e80597d88289df5f92c6286e10868378ec^{tree}` returns the same tree 760ec9c71336cffbf7a59cd84d6b7498343c992e for both, proving the decomposition corresponds to the landed squash.

`git show --format=fuller a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f -- src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs` shows that member commit adding ToJson, the static WriteValue function, and recursive calls for list elements and object member values, with no depth/cycle/stack control. `git log -S'WriteValue(context, writer, value)' a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f -- src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs` returns only a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f, cross-checking the smallest origin.

`git rev-parse a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f^` returns 0e777fe3c747e9ac4d774b8513e092ff3054ce34. Direct inspection with `git show 0e777fe3c747e9ac4d774b8513e092ff3054ce34:src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs` shows the class ending after Values and contains neither ToJson nor WriteValue, so the vulnerable implementation is absent in the immediate parent.

`git show --format=fuller 760dc21259f3da6a5adbd3148c260e25f1751706` shows the direct fix: it adds RuntimeHelpers.EnsureSufficientExecutionStack, ObjectRecursionLimit enforcement, and a reference-identity path HashSet, threads depth/path through both recursive calls, and adds cycle/depth regression tests. The immediate parent has the unguarded three-argument WriteValue. `git tag --contains 760dc21259f3da6a5adbd3148c260e25f1751706 --sort=version:refname` starts at 7.0.0; `git tag --contains f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1 --sort=version:refname` starts at 5.10.0. `git grep -n 'static void WriteValue' 6.6.0 7.0.0 -- src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs` shows the unguarded three-argument form in 6.6.0 and guarded depth/HashSet form in 7.0.0, independently establishing the release boundary despite the first-party advisory's inconsistent <=5.16.0 package-range display.

`git cat-file -p a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f` is the BIC-only AI check: author and committer are both René Larch <renelarch@gmail.com>; the object message contains only the feat subject and three implementation bullets, with no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, AI, Copilot, bot identity, or other AI marker. The later fix commit does have a Copilot co-author trailer, but the protocol excludes fix-only AI evidence from the BIC verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when the PR member a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f first creates object.to_json's unchecked recursive serializer; its direct parent lacks the entire function. The public squash is not the smallest BIC and was therefore decomposed to the retained, tree-equivalent PR chain. Commit 760dc21259f3da6a5adbd3148c260e25f1751706 directly closes both circular and deep-recursion paths before the 7.0.0 tag. Because the true BIC commit object identifies a human author/committer and has no AI marker or bot identity, the required BIC-only judgment is NOT_AI; Copilot attribution on the later fix is deliberately irrelevant.
